chapter_title_en: Meeting an Old Friend in a Strange Land
chapter_seo_title: Meeting an Old Friend in a Strange Land – Li Huowang Rejects a Disciple
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang encounters an old acquaintance in Yinling City and delivers a harsh severance, while a shocking discovery about Li Sui’s perception threatens the wall between reality and hallucination.
og_title: Severed Ties in a Strange Land – Li Huowang’s Cold Lesson
og_description: The Purple-Tasseled Sword bearer begs to follow, but Li Huowang cuts him loose with brutal efficiency—and a stray comment reveals Li Sui can hear the voices Li Huowang thought were only in his head.
twitter_title: He Cut Ties With His Student & the Hallucinations Got Realer
twitter_description: Li Huowang’s reunion with an old young disciple is anything but warm—but it’s the reveal that Li Sui can hear Red Center that will haunt you long after this chapter.

lore_anchors.definition: A ritual Daoist weapon composed of old Chinese coins strung on red thread. Each coin is believed to carry residual yang energy from circulation; removing a few still leaves the sword functional but weakened.
A parasitic entity that lives inside Li Huowang and has begun to develop intelligence and the ability to mimic voices. It calls him “Dad.”
One of the hallucinatory figures that follow Li Huowang. She is a jianghu woman who often comments on situations with cynical humor.
A prosperous city in the Da Liang empire where Li Huowang is currently staying at Tuoba Danqing’s suggestion.
The village where Li Huowang left his companions, including Bai Lingmiao and the Lü opera troupe.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Li Huowang refuse to take Lü Xiucai with him?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Because Lü Xiucai is a volatile, untrained liability. Li Huowang is hunted by gods, institutions, and his own mind—dragging a teenager along would endanger them both. He gives him travel money and a weapon, then cuts the cord decisively.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What does it mean that Li Sui can hear Red Center?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It suggests that Li Huowang’s hallucinations may have a reality that transcends his own perception. If a creature inside his body can hear the voices too, the line between “imagined” and “real” just got much thinner.
